AND PRINTS THE COMPARISON THEY MAKE
mm and MPa and cm²/m, in your unit convention · σₜ is the peak principal tension, dead load · Δ/L against Isler’s 1/300
These are real numbers, and they are the argument for the whole mode
Kresge Auditorium, Mekjavić & Pičulin (2010), Table 3. Distributing the same concrete — 8.9 cm everywhere, against a
thickness that grows to 30 cm at the three supports — takes the peak tension from 14.4 MPa to 3.9, and the deflection
from 299 mm to 50. The as-built shell sits at Δ/L = 1/164, four times worse than Isler’s 1/300 rule, and its snow case
fails in punching. Design 3 reaches 1/1340 and needs a fifth of the top steel.
So automatic thickening is not a tidying-up step. It is the design decision the tab exists to make — which is why it gets
a mode, a criterion you can name, limits you can build to, a convergence report, and this table.
